name: Oasis test (remembering beats sensing)
description: A small world for testing whether learning and memory can pay. Plants grow only in a handful of oases (about 5 to 9, covering 12 to 16% of the ground), with barren land 30 to 100 units wide between them, far beyond what an animal can smell (smell only compares the cells right beside it). Once an oasis is grazed bare, an animal can wander and hope, or head for an oasis it remembers. Brains can learn during life, remember up to four feeding places with a sense pointing to the best one elsewhere, and hold things in mind (working memory with hold gates); each ability is a gene that starts low and varies. Each oasis grows one of three kinds of plant, and the kinds peak at different times of year (growing almost nothing out of season), so food moves from oasis to oasis in a fixed yearly round, like a trapline. Every animal digests every kind, and the climate is the same everywhere. No home signal, so only memory (and the time-of-year sense) knows where and when food will be beyond sniffing distance.
